title: BIR Form No. 2200-C — Excise Tax Return for Cosmetic Procedures

choice_rows.label: Item 11 — Place where the invasive cosmetic procedures took place

validation.how: Messages render as text in a 'Needs review' section after Part III (first 20 only); a field only turns its label red, and Queue for submission is disabled with no message beside it.

lists.label: Part V Schedule 1 — Summary of Cosmetic Procedures Performed

findings.now: Print preview leaves all ten Schedule 1 rows blank and also drops Item 6, Items 9-10 and Item 11, so the paper copy shows only the Item 16 total.
findings.why: writer-cells.json has no join for the Schedule 1 product cells (left_out p2c25 onward, 'no printed row number or product label') nor for the RDO, contact/email and place combs.

options.name: Map rows by column order
options.detail: Join the ten Schedule 1 rows to the grid's column combs in order, since the row count is fixed at ten.

options.name: Print a generated table
options.detail: Append a table of columns A to J to the frozen sheet so the paper copy carries every entered value.

options.name: Warn before preview
options.detail: Show a notice naming Schedule 1 and Items 6, 9-11 as not on the frozen sheet until the grid is mapped.

findings.now: With any error the button greys out with no message beside it, the reason appears only under Needs review below Part III, and a bad Schedule 1 row turns no row field red.
findings.why: The button is disabled whenever validation_errors or parse_errors is non-empty, and field() matches only exact keys such as ca0, so the schedule[n] error from validate() never highlights its row.

options.name: Inline message per field
options.detail: Show the alert text directly under the failing field instead of only in the panel.

options.name: Toolbar summary
options.detail: Show the first error text beside Queue for submission so the disabled button still explains itself.

options.name: Keep enabled and scroll
options.detail: Let a click scroll to Needs review and highlight the first failing row instead of greying out.

findings.field: Item 11 — Place where the invasive cosmetic procedures took place
findings.now: Each Region, Province and City choice opens a wrap of outline buttons on the page (17 regions, up to 7 provinces per region, up to 53 cities per province).
findings.why: A button list this long is hard to scan, and 2200M and 2200P already use a searchable combobox for their Region, Province and City choices.

options.name: Combobox
options.detail: A searchable select per level, the same control the 2200M place_block uses.

options.name: Read-only chip
options.detail: Show the chosen place as one chip and open the picker only when the filer chooses Change.

findings.now: Item 1 Month is a row of twelve small buttons, and opening the form from the library ignores the dashboard period, so the date starts as today or as 12/31 in other years.
findings.why: The official page uses a month dropdown (BIR-Form2200Cv2018.hta:411), and new_draft discards the period argument.

options.name: Combobox
options.detail: A twelve-item select matching the official month dropdown.

options.name: Segmented control
options.detail: Keep buttons only if all twelve fit one row at desktop width.

findings.now: The RDO shows as bold text taken from the profile with no control on this page, yet a missing or invalid value blocks queueing with 'Please enter a valid RDO Code on Page 1 Item 6.'
findings.why: The official page offers an RDO dropdown in div#rdoContainer (BIR-Form2200Cv2018.hta:525-527) that the filer can change, while the port renders it as read-only text.

options.name: Dropdown
options.detail: Offer the official RDO list as a searchable select bound to the draft's rdo_code.

options.name: Read-only with profile link
options.detail: Keep it fixed but link the chip to the profile setting that owns the RDO.

findings.now: After the form reloads, Schedule 1 boxes show raw numbers such as 50010 or 1234.5, while the money boxes show grouped two-decimal amounts such as 1,234.00.
findings.why: initial() formats schedule cells with format!("{value}") instead of official_amount, so they are not rounded or grouped like formatCurrency.

options.name: official_amount
options.detail: Reuse the formatter the money boxes and computed rows already use.

options.name: Format on blur
options.detail: Show the raw value while typing and the official_amount text when the box loses focus.

findings.now: Typing 100 or more into Item 1 Day, or 10000 or more into Item 1 Year, shows the 'is required' alert instead of the official date or year alert.
findings.why: sync_from_inputs maps out-of-range numbers to 0 (day range 0-99, year range 0-9999), and validate() reports a zero as a missing field.

options.name: Pass the typed number through
options.detail: Let validate() raise the valid-date alert that the official validateDate raises.

options.name: Limit the boxes
options.detail: Cap typing at two digits for Day and four for Year, as the official maxlength does.

findings.now: When more than twenty messages exist, the Needs review section silently stops at the twentieth.
findings.why: The .take(20) call drops the remaining messages with no count and no more note.

options.name: Show all
options.detail: Remove the cap, since the page already scrolls.

options.name: Count note
options.detail: Keep twenty and add a '+N more' line under the list.

findings.now: A malformed address such as 'abc' is reported as 'E-mail address on page 1 item 10 is required.', and 'a@b' passes validation.
findings.why: validate() only checks for an '@' and no whitespace, so it uses the mandatory-field text for a format failure, unlike the 2200M and 2200P pages that apply the official pattern.

options.name: Official pattern
options.detail: Reuse email_matches_official_pattern with the official text 'Please enter a valid e-mail address on page 1 item 10'.

options.name: Presence only
options.detail: Match the 2200C HTA, which defines validateEmail (BIR-Form2200Cv2018.hta:3554) but never calls it, and drop the '@' rule.
